extracted.intended_audience: startup founders, PR/communications and marketing teams preparing funding announcement press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a template for writing and distributing a startup funding announcement press release that clearly states amount, use of funds, investor thesis, customer validation, and distribution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline formula
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company] Raises $[Amount] to [Specific Use of Funds]"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a headline that names the company, the dollar amount, and a specific use of funds. Examples from the page: "Acme Raises $20M to Expand AI-Powered Inventory to Europe", "BetaCorp Raises $50M to Build Out 200-Person Engineering Team", "Gamma Raises $5M Seed to Launch Climate-Tech Marketplace". Avoid generic headlines that only state the amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede formula
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company], a [brief description], today announced $[amount] in [round type] funding led by [lead investor], with participation from [other investors]. The funds will be used to [specific use]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the release with a single-paragraph lede that hits company description, amount, round type, lead investor and participants, and the specific use of funds. Make the lede factual and specific so reporters can quickly understand the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-funds — hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring (specific numbers, specific roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concrete hiring plans (e.g., "hire 100 engineers in Berlin"), naming role types and headcount where possible — this gives credibility and signals company priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-funds — product development
rubrics_metrics.description: Product development (specific roadmap items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific product initiatives that the funding will enable (e.g., features, platform launches, technical milestones) rather than vague 'product improvements.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-funds — geographic expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic expansion (specific markets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the markets or regions being targeted (e.g., "expand to Europe, starting with Germany and the UK") rather than 'expand internationally.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-funds — customer acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer acquisition (specific channels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify acquisition channels and strategies (e.g., enterprise partnerships, paid digital channels, channel sales) so the use of funds reads as a concrete go-to-market plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-funds — R&D
rubrics_metrics.description: R&D in specific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funds are for R&D, name the research areas or technologies (e.g., machine learning model development, materials research) to show focused investment rather than generic R&D spend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor quote — lead investor only
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead investor only; substantive reasoning behind investment; specific market thesis; why this team; why now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a quote from the lead investor that explains the investment thesis and why they backed the company now. Avoid short platitudes or cheerleading; focus on market insights, team strengths, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO quote — milestone and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the milestone briefly; focus on what the funding enables; specific upcoming priorities; customer focus; honest about challenges remaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEO quotes should be forward-looking and practical: mention priorities the funds enable, customer outcomes, and be candid about next challenges. Avoid generic exclamations like "We're excited."

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer/partner validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Named customer with quote; specific use case; measurable outcome; industry relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a quoted endorsement from a named customer or partner that explains how they use the product and the measurable benefit (metrics, outcomes). This provides third-party validation and relevance to the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief company description; founded date and headquarters; total raised to date; number of customers/users; mission in one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate concise but fact-filled: founding info, HQ, cumulative funding, customer/user counts, and a one-sentence mission. This is the evergreen company summary for journalists to reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia (team photos, product screenshots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images and screenshots that journalists can use. Multimedia increases pickup and makes the story more engaging; include captions and usage guidance if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder availability for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder available for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make founders and spokespeople available soon after release; provide contact info and windows of availability to facilitate coverage and follow-up reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — embargoed exclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed exclusive to top trade outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer an embargoed exclusive to a top trade outlet to secure feature coverage, then coordinate secondary distribution. Ensure embargo terms are clear and respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — coordinated secondary outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinated release to 5-10 secondary outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a coordinated outreach to a set of secondary trade and local outlets (5–10) to expand coverage beyond the exclusive while maintaining timing control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — wire syndication after initial coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire syndication for SEO (after initial coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire services for broad SEO value and long-tail pickup, but syndicate after initial exclusive/earned coverage to avoid spoiling exclusives and to maximize top-outlet visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — founder/CEO social announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder/CEO LinkedIn announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders should post on LinkedIn (and other relevant social channels) to amplify coverage and reach networks — coordinate timing with embargoes and media pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — investor co-promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor co-promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask lead investors to help amplify the announcement via their channels to reach additional audiences and lend credibility; coordinate messaging and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: generic headline 'Company Raises $X'
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline that's just "Company Raises $X" is ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This type of headline gives no signal about use of funds or company direction. Prefer the headline formula that includes specific use of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: 'We're excited' CEO quote
rubrics_metrics.description: "We're excited" CEO quote is a weak, overused platitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace generic enthusiasm with concrete statements about what the funding enables and upcoming priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: promotional investor cheerleading quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor quotes that are mere promotional cheerleading add little value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage investors to provide a substantive investment thesis or market insight rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: no use-of-funds clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: No use-of-funds clarity undermines the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how funds will be spent (hiring, product, markets, channels) — vagueness reduces reporter and market confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: wire-only distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire-only distribution is insufficient and often ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying only on wire services typically yields weak coverage; combine exclusives, targeted outreach, and social amplification instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid: no customer or product validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of customer or product validation weakens credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one named customer/partner quote or concrete product usage metrics to demonstrate traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — headline includes specific use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline includes specific use of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appears in the page's explicit 'Quality Rubric for Funding Announcements' as a top-line checklist item; verify the headline follows the Headline Formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — use of funds detailed in body
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funds detailed in body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body must include specific uses (hiring, product, markets, channels, R&D); cross-check with the Use-of-Funds Specifics entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — substantive investor quote with thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive investor quote with thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the investor quote explains the market thesis and rationale rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — customer validation included
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer validation included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm at least one named customer or partner quote, with a specific use case or measurable outcome.
